description: For each archetype, the complete set of AWS services that could potentially serve the workload. CONSTRAIN narrows this pool by removing impossible options; RESOLVE picks the winner from what remains.

container.notes: Fargate is the default for containerized workloads. Lambda if event-driven + short. EC2 if GPU/high-resource. EKS if K8s required.

function.notes: Lambda is the default for functions. Fargate if timeout >15min or unsupported runtime.

vm.notes: EC2 is the default for VMs. Fargate if containerizable + cost-sensitive.

kubernetes.notes: EKS if K8s preference explicit. Fargate if no K8s preference (simpler managed containers).

app-engine.notes: Fargate is the default. Lambda if purely event-driven handlers.

relational-db.notes: RDS for single-az/multi-az. Aurora for multi-az-ha/multi-region. Family selected by availability (Q6).

nosql-document.notes: DynamoDB is the sole target unless >100 txn items (eliminator → RDS fallback).

cache.notes: Redis is the default (direct-mapped). Memcached only if explicitly simple key-value with no persistence.

distributed-relational.notes: Aurora DSQL for global strong consistency. Aurora for single-region. DynamoDB if key-value dominant.
